idea-plugin.name: Zacess Themes
idea-plugin.description:
Ten accessible themes: four match the Zacess reader, so a page looks the same in the reader and in the IDE, four give the highest contrast a screen can show and the Warm pair is a gentler option for anyone who finds high contrast too intense.

  • Zacess Light: Ink on white, the reader's Dark on light theme.
  • Zacess Dark: Near white on near black, the reader's Light on dark theme.
  • Zacess Yellow on Black: Yellow on black for low vision, the reader's Yellow on black theme.
  • Zacess Cream: Black on cream for dyslexia, the reader's Black on cream theme.
  • Zacess High Contrast Dark: White on black with strong borders and a yellow focus ring, for the highest contrast on a dark screen.
  • Zacess High Contrast Light: Black on white with strong dark borders and focus outlines, for the highest contrast on a light screen.
  • Zacess Deep Contrast Dark: White on black with deep, fully saturated colours, yellow focus outlines and cyan frames, for low vision.
  • Zacess Deep Contrast Light: Black on white with vivid deep colours, red focus outlines and navy frames, for low vision.
  • Zacess Warm Dark: Cream on warm dark brown with earthy amber, rust, olive and teal, a gentler theme for anyone who finds high contrast too intense.
  • Zacess Warm Light: Dark brown on warm paper with earthy amber, rust, olive and teal, a gentler theme for anyone who finds high contrast too intense.

Every text and syntax colour keeps at least 7:1 contrast (WCAG AAA) on the background. Zacess Warm Dark and Zacess Warm Light keep 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) instead. The current line is a visible band with plain text at the theme's text floor and every syntax colour at 4.5:1 or more over it. Comments are never dimmed below that floor. Selected text takes one colour at the floor or more on a bold selection block. Keywords are bold, comments italic and invalid code underlined, so colour is never the only signal.

Source, contrast tables and issues: https://github.com/zacesshq/themes
